disease_label_per_paper: Trichinellosis-induced eosinophilic myocarditis mimicking hypereosinophilic syndrome

demographics.country_or_region_context: Patient returned from travel to the Philippines

presentation_summary: A 59-year-old man with known bicuspid aortic valve disease reported eating raw pork while traveling in the Philippines.
In the months after return he developed recurrent syncope, severe progressively worsening symmetric proximal myalgias and weakness, and pleuritic chest pain.

He presented in cardiogenic shock; initial echocardiography showed preserved left ventricular ejection fraction of 55-60% but new severe aortic stenosis physiology requiring vasopressors and emergent balloon valvuloplasty, then transcatheter aortic valve replacement after severe aortic insufficiency developed.
Inflammatory markers, troponin, leukocytosis, and hypereosinophilia continued to rise despite initial stabilization.
Ventricular tachycardia caused cardiac arrest with return of spontaneous circulation.
Rectus femoris muscle biopsy showed chronic endomysial and perivascular inflammation with focal eosinophils and parasitic organisms morphologically consistent with Trichinella spiralis.
Albendazole, ivermectin for incidental Strongyloides IgG positivity, and methylprednisolone were given, followed by complete resolution of the critical illness.

risk_context.source_text_value: Admitted consumption of raw pork during travel to the Philippines
Known bicuspid aortic valve followed by cardiology before travel
Strongyloides IgG index value was positive at 2.3

observations.source_text_value: Consumption of raw pork in the Philippines
Severe progressively worsening symmetric proximal myalgias
Severe progressively worsening symmetric proximal weakness
Mean gradient across the aortic valve was 78 mmHg
No directed anthelmintic therapy before muscle biopsy diagnosis

values.source_text_value: Troponin increased to 1,466 ng/L at peak

imaging.finding: LVEF 55-60%, normal right ventricular function, new severe aortic stenosis physiology with valve area 0.8 cm2, mean gradient 78 mmHg, peak velocity 5.6 m/s, and no aortic regurgitation initially.
Development of pericardial effusion while chest pain persisted.

diagnostics.result: Scattered foci of chronic endomysial and perivascular inflammation with focal increased eosinophils and parasitic organisms morphologically consistent with Trichinella spiralis.
Index value 2.3, reported as incidental positivity; ivermectin was included in directed therapy.

clinical_course.event: Presented in cardiogenic shock requiring vasopressors and emergent balloon valvuloplasty.
Mean aortic valve gradient improved from 87 to 35 mmHg after valvuloplasty, but severe aortic insufficiency required transcatheter aortic valve replacement.
Ventricular tachycardia caused cardiac arrest with return of spontaneous circulation.
High-dose pulse methylprednisolone was started for suspected eosinophilic myocarditis, eosinophilic polymyositis, and hypereosinophilic syndrome.
Directed albendazole, ivermectin, and methylprednisolone resulted in complete resolution of critical illness.

actual_treatment: Emergent balloon valvuloplasty and transcatheter aortic valve replacement for severe aortic valve physiology.
High-dose pulse methylprednisolone for eosinophilic myocarditis / polymyositis inflammatory syndrome.
Ivermectin was also given because Strongyloides IgG was incidentally positive.
Aspirin and clopidogrel were used after valvuloplasty/TAVR.

outcome.source_text_value: Further directed therapy resulted in complete resolution of the critical illness.

quality_warnings: Cardiogenic shock and ventricular tachycardia are preserved as clinical-course events rather than converted into arbitrary daily event-rate values.

Strongyloides seropositivity is retained as coinfection/prior exposure context but expected_manifold remains D-TRICHINELLOSIS because biopsy showed Trichinella organisms and the paper diagnosis was trichinellosis-induced myocarditis.
